title: correction signals counted DSH-injected user-role records as user pushback

evidence.excerpt: # Handoff: Build `/self-improve` for dshfiles ## Objective Implement a `/self-improve` skill that allows our DSH-based ADE to **learn from its own historical sessions and continuously improve the agent harness, workflows, tools, skills, pro

<system-reminder> The following workspace instructions may be relevant to your work. Use them as guidance when applicable. More specific instructions take precedence over broader ones. They do not override system, developer, or direct user

<system-reminder> A skill is a reusable set of task-specific instructions. The following skills are available in this session: <available_skills> - `actor-state-ownership`: Design frontend state machines and actors with explicit ownership,

rootCause: Prompt origin was guessed from message text and index; DSH marks it structurally in data.source.kind, and appends runtime context, the skill catalog, compaction checkpoints, background-job notices and peer-agent messages as user-role records.
hypothesis: Classifying prompts by data.source.kind (only 'user' is human) and by whether the agent has produced output yet removes the false corrections without losing genuine pushback.

experiments.hypothesis: Classifying a user-role record by its structural origin (data.source.kind; only 'user' is human) and by whether the agent has already produced output removes false correction signals without losing genuine pushback.
experiments.baseline: extractor version 1 over the same 14-day corpus, saved as output/self-improve/baseline-before-fix.json before the change
experiments.metric: Sessions and hits per correction signal, coverage.totalCorrections, and the presence of turn-end:completed
experiments.before: misunderstood-requirement 631 sessions/1943 hits; process-complaint 56/103; incomplete-or-unfixed 631/3979; unwanted-change 70/128; coverage.totalCorrections 4095; turn-end:completed 601/2960
experiments.after: misunderstood-requirement 24/29; process-complaint 2/2; incomplete-or-unfixed 130/188; unwanted-change 23/23; coverage.totalCorrections 224; turn-end:completed not reported
experiments.conditions: Same DSH_HOME and 14-day window, harness unchanged, extractor version 1 to 4. The corpus grew from 806 to 810 analyzed Sessions between the runs, which is why the two control signals drift slightly and why 'after' is not exactly reproducible today.

title: apply_patch fails with "cannot get property workingDirectory without inject"

evidence.excerpt: Error: cannot get property "workingDirectory" without inject
Error: cannot get property "workingDirectory" without inject
Error: cannot get property "workingDirectory" without inject

rootCause: The tool handler reads context.workingDirectory off execution.agent.ctx (plugins/@dshfiles/apply-patch/src/patch-tool.ts:84). Cordis raises this error when the property is not provided by an inject declaration on the fiber that serves that ctx, so the plugin-level inject in host.ts does not reach the per-agent context the tool executes with.
hypothesis: Reading the service with a nullable lookup (ctx.get("workingDirectory")) or injecting it on the tool execution context removes 453 failures per week without changing patch semantics.

history.note: recorded from non-Session evidence

Root cause confirmed: the tool body resolved its context from execution.agent.ctx, and that scoped Agent context does not inject workingDirectory. Rebuilt the tool from the plugin context and register it from setup; regression test fails if the Agent context is read again.
Landed on main as jj:nopxrltu (53f9d8f). The entry is referenced by change id so a rebase cannot orphan it.

title: bash calls over 30s grew 1,046 → 2,830 across 307 Sessions

evidence.excerpt: bash took 30s+ on 2 of 54 calls (worst 45.7s) (1046 → 2830 hits, 307 Sessions)

rootCause: Not established as a defect: a bash call over 30 s is the shape of a test run, a build or a blocking wait, and the tool has no timeout of its own. The 2026-10-24 review shows the growth, not its cause.
hypothesis: Most of the growth is long test/build commands and waits that belong in a background job; instruction-level guidance would move a minority, and a tool-level change is not justified without per-command attribution.

history.note: recorded from non-Session evidence
Measured as volume only, not attributed per command. Reopen when a review can attribute the slow calls by command family or job kind; then choose between guidance and a tool seam.

Error: API schema validation failed: commitId: Invalid string: must match pattern /^(?:[a-f0-9]{40}|[a-f0-9]{64})$/.
Error: API schema validation failed: commitId: Invalid string: must match pattern /^(?:[a-f0-9]{40}|[a-f0-9]{64})$/.

rootCause: jj_details requires a 40- or 64-character hexadecimal commit hash, while agents pass short prefixes supported by many jj CLI commands; the schema rejects these before revision lookup.
hypothesis: Explicit guidance to use a full commit hash for jj_details, resolving it with jj logs or jj_load first, will prevent this recurring schema error.

experiments.hypothesis: Guidance to pass full hexadecimal commit hashes to jj_details prevents schema validation failures caused by short prefixes.
experiments.baseline: Previous week had no sampled jj_details commitId schema failures; current week had 80 failures across 45 Sessions.
experiments.metric: jj_details schema-validation failures in the next weekly Session-log review
experiments.before: 80 failures across 45 Sessions during 2026-10-18 through 2026-10-25; sampled source calls used short commit prefixes (e.g. af242a61).
experiments.after: Not yet measurable; the guidance has just been added.
experiments.conditions: Observational weekly review, no controlled counterfactual; future workload and Session mix may differ.
